title: Building an Immersive Language Learning RPG
author: nikkileaps
selftext:
I've been working on **Wordlark Hollow**, an immersive language-learning RPG where the idea is that reading and communicating in the language you're learning is actually part of playing the game.

One of the things I've been working on most is the conversation system because I don't want a game kinda' like painted over a flashcard system. I don't want players choosing from three canned dialogue responses - I want them to be able to type whatever they actually want to say and to be using their target language as much as possible.

The trickiest part has been avoiding completely generative NPCs. The characters, world, quests and major dialogue beats are authored, but I also still want free conversation to be possible. AI sits inside that structure and helps interpret what the learner is trying to say and generate an appropriate in-character response. The newest Claude models have been a real game changer for some of it.

It's been fascinating and surprisingly fun. I actually don't mind play testing the same thing for the 100th time because the characters will still say funny and slightly different things and I get to kind of live in this world I'm inventing. And as I am tuning it and writing more and more of their lore ( the part I really love! ) they get richer and more ... character-like I guess if that makes any sense?  
  
Finally gotten far enough along and gotten enough positive, yes-I-have-also-been-trying-to-learn-Italian-for-years in Dulingo lol that I launched a Kickstarter this week: [https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/nikkileaps/wordlark-hollow](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/nikkileaps/wordlark-hollow)  
  
Anyways I'm curious how other people here are handling and exploring the balance between player freedom and authored narrative.
